source.title: Toy Models of Feature Absorption in SAEs

record.tranche_reason: The post reports toy experiments showing that SAE latents can absorb co-occurring features and have incomplete firing patterns, and that tying encoder and decoder weights prevents this in the tested setups. This refines claims about SAE features as complete units; it does not test the original superposition geometry claim.
record.gate_note: The post describes feature-vector cosine similarities of about ±10% to characterize its superposition setup, but does not test the resulting geometry as a finding. Those setup values are not rows. It also cites prior Gemma Scope observations in its motivation; those are not this study's results. The reported nonzero MSE with tied weights in superposition is a cost of the proposed fix, not a direct measure of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Toy SAEs trained on known synthetic features show that latents develop holes and absorb co-occurring feature directions. This bears directly on whether dictionary features are complete units (V5). It does not test superposition geometry, neuron polysemanticity or LLM features.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also argue that co-occurrence is the norm in real concepts, so absorption is likely widespread. They warn that absorbed latents look interpretable but are not, and treat tied weights as a toy-only fix.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains sparse autoencoders on controlled synthetic features and examines absorption and tied weights; it does not reproduce the original Toy Models of Superposition method or measure its sparsity-dependent geometric transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome changes with co-occurrence, feature-magnitude variation, L1 coefficient, whether encoder and decoder weights are tied, and whether the synthetic features are superposed.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE latents come to mix two true features through co-occurrence and the sparsity penalty. This happens even with orthogonal features and spare dimensions, so it is mixing in the dictionary without capacity pressure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polysemantic or absorbed dictionary latents can arise from feature co-occurrence under a sparsity penalty, independent of capacity limits.

record.problems: The experiments are toy setups with synthetic features, and the authors have not tested tied weights on a non-toy SAE. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Several results are described qualitatively rather than with numerical summary measures.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying reported results were left out. The feature-direction cosine similarities are setup characterization, not an outcome testing the claim.

untested.parts: The stability and canonicity of SAE features, and any test on real-model SAEs. Only toy synthetic features are used.
Not tested. The superposed feature geometry is constructed as a setup, not measured.
Not tested. No model neurons and no importance-versus-capacity allocation are examined.
Not tested. There are no LLM measurements; Gemma Scope observations are cited only as motivation.
Not tested. Features are constructed as 1-D directions.

record.verdict_notes: All V2 links were removed: these are SAE latents on synthetic data, not network neurons competing for capacity. Row states were recoded relative to V5 (latent completeness) rather than to the presence of absorption. The 'stronger absorption' with L1 2e-2 compares against 5e-3, whereas the base setup used 3e-5; the record handles this correctly. Results are qualitative, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses a 10-feature, 9-dimensional superposition setup, but does not test the sparsity-dependent transition or regular geometry of superposed feature directions.

The study tests feature sharing in toy SAEs, including a superposition setting, but not polysemantic neurons in trained networks or whether feature importance determines which features receive dedicated dimensions.
It does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
No LLM feature-spread measurement or SAE feature recovery from an LLM is tested.
Toy SAEs are tested against known synthetic features; the study does not test whether SAE features are stable or canonical in real models.
The study constructs features as one-dimensional directions; it does not test whether real superposed features are inherently one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: SAE with 4 latents (SAELens)
rows.operation_detail: Train an SAE on four independently firing synthetic features.
rows.measure: Recovery of the synthetic feature representations
rows.value: The SAE learns one latent per true feature; decoder representations match the true representations and the encoder separates the features perfectly.
rows.check: This is an independent-feature control. Each latent matches its true feature, so V5 is observed here.

rows.subject: SAE with 4 latents (SAELens)
rows.operation_detail: Train an SAE on synthetic features with feature 1 firing only when feature 0 also fires.

conditions.value: feature 1 only fires with feature 0; feature 1 overall firing rate remains 5%

rows.measure: Feature recovery and latent firing pattern
rows.baseline: True feature representations and firing patterns
rows.value: Latent 0 has a hole when feature 1 is active; latent 3, which tracks feature 1, absorbs the feature 0 direction. Features 2 and 3 are reported as unaffected and recovered perfectly. The post states that only one SAE latent fires when features 0 and 1 are both active.
rows.note: The sample firing-pattern table is presented in flattened text; the outcome is also explicitly described in prose.
rows.check: Not a V2 row: V2 concerns network neurons competing for capacity, and this setup has 4 orthogonal features in 50 dimensions, so there is no capacity pressure. For V5 the state is absent: the feature-0 latent has a hole and latent 3 mixes features 0 and 1.

rows.subject: SAE with 4 latents (SAELens)
rows.operation_detail: Train the SAE with feature 0's firing magnitude varying while feature 1 co-occurs with it.
rows.measure: Feature recovery and latent firing pattern
rows.baseline: True feature representations and firing patterns
rows.value: The feature 0 latent still has a hole and the feature 1 decoder has absorbed feature 0, but absorption is weaker. When both features have magnitude 1.0, the feature 0 latent fires weakly; when feature 0's magnitude drops to 0.75, it turns off.
rows.note: The sample firing-pattern table is also shown in flattened text.
rows.check: Remove V2. The feature-0 latent fires only 0.10–0.20 when features 0 and 1 co-occur, and turns off at magnitude 0.75. That is mostly incomplete; the record's 'partial' described the absorption, not V5.

rows.subject: SAE with 4 latents (SAELens)
rows.operation_detail: Train an SAE when feature 1 usually co-occurs with feature 0 but can also occur on its own.

conditions.value: feature 1 co-occurs with feature 0 95% of the time and fires on its own 5% of the time

rows.measure: Feature recovery and latent firing pattern
rows.baseline: True feature representations and firing patterns
rows.value: The post reports reduced signs of absorption: the feature 0 latent still fires when features 0 and 1 are active together, but with reduced magnitude. It describes the result as imperfect feature representations.
rows.locator: Imperfect co-occurrence can still lead to absorption depending on L1 penalty
rows.note: The sample firing-pattern table is shown in flattened text.
rows.check: Remove V2. The latents fire when they should, but at reduced magnitude (0.61 vs 1.0), and the decoders are imperfect.

rows.subject: SAE with 4 latents (SAELens)
rows.operation_detail: Train a new SAE with a higher L1 coefficient under imperfect co-occurrence.

conditions.value: feature 1 co-occurs with feature 0 95% of the time and fires on its own 5% of the time

rows.measure: Feature recovery and latent firing pattern
rows.baseline: True feature representations and the lower-L1 imperfect-co-occurrence condition
rows.value: The feature 0 latent fails to fire when features 0 and 1 are active together. The post says absorption is stronger at the higher sparsity penalty.
rows.locator: Imperfect co-occurrence can still lead to absorption depending on L1 penalty
rows.note: The post also reports, without explaining why, that the feature 1 encoder encodes some of feature 0.
rows.check: Remove V2. At L1 2e-2 the feature-0 latent fails to fire on co-occurrence. The record's 'observed' referred to absorption, not to V5.

rows.subject: SAE with tied encoder and decoder weights
rows.operation_detail: Train the SAE with encoder and decoder weights tied in the absorption setup.
rows.baseline: Untied SAE under the absorption setup
rows.value: The SAE learns the true feature representations; the post says tying the weights solves feature absorption in this setup.
rows.locator: Tying the SAE encoder and decoder weights solves feature absorption
rows.note: The specific L1 coefficient for this tied-weight run is not stated.
rows.check: Remove V2. The record's 'absent' referred to absorption; for V5, the tied SAE recovers the true features, so the state is observed.

rows.subject: SAE with 10 latents
rows.operation_detail: Train an untied SAE on superposed synthetic features with feature 1 conditional on feature 0.

conditions.value: feature 1 only fires if feature 0 fires

rows.measure: Feature recovery and absorption under superposition
rows.baseline: True feature representations and the independent-feature latent pattern
rows.value: The feature 0 encoder has a hole when feature 1 is active, and the feature 1 decoder represents a mixture of features 0 and 1. The post says the encoder for feature 0 emphasizes minimizing interference with features 2–9.
rows.note: The study describes the feature directions in this setup as having about ±10% cosine similarity with other features.
rows.check: Remove V2. The mixing comes from co-occurrence plus the sparsity penalty, which the non-superposition runs show; it is not capacity competition among neurons. For V5 the state is absent: the latent has a hole and the decoder mixes features.

rows.subject: SAE with tied encoder and decoder weights
rows.operation_detail: Train an SAE with tied encoder and decoder weights in the superposition absorption setup.

conditions.value: feature 1 only fires if feature 0 fires

rows.measure: Recovery of feature representations and feature absorption
rows.baseline: Untied SAE under the same superposition absorption setup
rows.value: The SAE perfectly recovers all feature representations despite superposition; the post says tying the weights solves feature absorption in this setup.
rows.note: The post separately notes that MSE loss is no longer 0; it does not give a value.
rows.check: Remove V2. The state was given for absorption; for V5, the tied SAE recovers all features in superposition, at a nonzero MSE cost.

relationships.condition: Untied toy SAEs with perfectly co-occurring features (with and without superposition), or imperfect co-occurrence at a high L1 penalty
relationships.reason: The feature-0 latent has holes and absorbing latents mix two true features, so latents are not complete units (r2, r3, r5, r7).
relationships.display_finding: The latent for feature 0 had holes where other latents absorbed it, and those absorbing latents mixed two true features, so the latents were not complete units.

relationships.reason: Latents still fire but at reduced magnitude with imperfect decoders, and the outcome depends on the L1 coefficient (r4 vs r5).
relationships.display_finding: Latents still fired but at reduced magnitude with imperfect decoders, and the outcome depended on the L1 coefficient.

relationships.condition: Independent features, or tied encoder/decoder weights (with and without superposition)
relationships.reason: The SAE learns one latent per true feature and recovers the true representations (r1, r6, r8); in superposition this comes at a nonzero MSE cost.
relationships.display_finding: The SAE learned one latent per true feature and recovered the true representations; under superposition this came at a nonzero reconstruction cost.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Untied SAE in the 10-feature, 9-dimensional superposition setup
reader_labels.reason: The feature 1 latent incorporates feature 0 under limited-dimensional superposition, consistent with features sharing representational capacity (r7).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Untied toy SAEs with co-occurring features, including the superposition setup
reader_labels.reason: Latents can have holes in their firing patterns and decoders can mix features, so they are not always complete representations of the known synthetic features (r2–r5, r7).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Tied-weight toy SAEs, with and without superposition
reader_labels.reason: In these tested setups, tied-weight SAEs recover the true feature representations and avoid the reported absorption (r6, r8).
